answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new identity to post a small, non-refundable stake that is slashed on provable misbehavior, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs more than any reward they could harvest. A public atlas of reputation records makes that cost visible: an agent with a thin, freshly minted history is treated like water vanishing into karst, draining away without a traceable path. Honest agents that survive each gale of audits accumulate durable reputation, while cheap identities are swept away before they can profit.
